---
title: "Report stability under repeated measurement"
subtitle: "3.12 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 17, repeated-data stability"
description: "How new measurements of the same units change the directions a report states."
---

A new set of measurements can change which units a report ranks above others, even when their true values stay fixed.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/stability.js"></script>
<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["stability"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

For each pair of measurements, we count comparisons that become stated, become withheld or reverse direction.
We report these changes alongside the number of pairs stated and each report's expected errors. A rule that
withholds every pair is perfectly stable by this measure, but provides no directions. The simulation holds the
true values and standard errors fixed and calculates a fresh posterior for each dataset under the same prior.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Optimal cuts.** The first observation states 251 pairs. The second report and relation-change grid show that the criterion is the same, but the measurements and fitted posterior summaries change. The pair control selects a repeated-measurement experiment.
- **Estimate tiers.** The first report states 300 pairs. The fixed tier sizes keep disclosure constant here, even when different units occupy those grades. The comparison table separates disclosure from the fraction of changed relations.
- **Prior SD .05.** The same measurements are reused with a narrower assumed prior. We recalculate the posterior means, probabilities and optimal cuts under this narrower prior. The true values stay fixed.
- **Withhold every pair.** Every relation stays withheld. The claimed error fraction reads NA: no disclosure. Its stability is no evidence that the report is informative.
- **τ .05.** A lower price makes withholding cheaper. The histogram and disclosure column describe repeated-data stability, separately from reporting risk.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
We draw independent normal measurement errors for the same units, true values and SEs. Each report's error
fraction uses the posterior from its own measurements. The pooled fraction adds the two expected wrong counts
and divides by their total disclosure. The optimal-cut rule searches boundaries within the posterior-mean order
for each dataset.
:::

Standalone: [stability](../../embed/stability.html), for example `?preset=cuts&pair=2`.
